name: Rocker on/off switch (KCD1)
summary: The small square rocker switch found on power strips. Clips into a 19 x 13 mm rectangular hole, no screws needed.
source: KCD1 is a shape that many factories copy rather than a controlled standard, so the numbers move. The 19.0 x 13.0 mm snap-in cutout is what the common KCD1-101 wants and is the size most sellers quote, but parts also sold as KCD1 exist with a 21 x 15 mm cutout, and the illuminated versions are usually deeper. Nothing behind the panel is verified: housing depth, terminal type (solder lug or 4.8 mm spade) and terminal length all vary. Check the cutout drawing that came with your switch, and test-fit in scrap before cutting the real panel.

keepouts.label: Room for the front bezel and the rocker to tilt
Room for the terminals and wires behind the panel

electrical.note: Typically rated 6 A at 250 V AC or 10 A at 125 V AC. These are usually wired to mains, which is dangerous: insulate the terminals and keep them out of reach.
